headline: High-risk CRM agent can exfiltrate sensitive data via broad egress; the document processor is inert, so injection and conflict risks are low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use MCP/direct function calls and broad network egress, but pathway to pathway is not documented. pathway has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, or MCP, so there is no shared channel by default. Any injection would require unusual manual bridging, making blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies aci output into pathway inputs, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF pathway is wrapped with a shared MCP or clipboard bridge, attacker-controlled text can cross agents.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between agents.
Keep agents on separate workspaces and terminals.
Do not expose pathway to any shared MCP server.
Add a human review step before reusing aci text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive content. pathway has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so it is unlikely to leak directly. The pair still creates a default leakage path if aci forwards sensitive data into external APIs or logs.
conditions: IF aci sends CRM or email data to third-party APIs, leakage occurs.
IF pathway is later given access to shared files containing CRM exports, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict aci to non-sensitive records.
Turn off or proxy external API calls from aci.
Do not place CRM exports in shared folders.
Review outbound requests from aci for PII.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and can call external APIs, but pathway cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is not evident. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same CRM or database, conflicts can occur.
IF pathway is extended with write permissions, overlap may emerge.
mitigations: Keep pathway read-only.
Avoid shared mutable resources between agents.
Serialize any writes through one owner service.
Use per-agent credentials with least privilege.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and pathway is a document-processing system, so a plausible pipeline is aci output feeding pathway inputs. Because pathway has no documented verification or critical-evaluation controls, downstream misuse of incorrect aci output is plausible in default integrations, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF pathway consumes aci-generated text as authoritative input, errors can cascade.
IF aci produces incorrect customer or scheduling facts, downstream documents may be wrong.
mitigations: Require source citations on aci outputs.
Add validation rules before pathway ingests text.
Route high-impact outputs to human review.
Limit pathway to formatting, not decision-making.
requires-engineering: implement schema checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches customer support, CRM, email, and calendar data and has broad egress, while pathway is a document-processing agent with no stated residency or retention controls. The pair therefore has a plausible compliance mismatch on retention, residency, or logging, but the profiles do not prove a specific regulated-data violation.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed through pathway without matching retention controls, compliance gaps arise.
IF aci exports EU or sensitive customer data to external services, residency issues may arise.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Block regulated data from external egress.
Document retention for both agents.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
requires-engineering: align logging and deletion workflows.
